article.dek: Friday's final injury reports are in — Darnold is cleared, Stanley is out, Flowers is a game-time call — and all three of the app's headline cards shuffled overnight.

bullets: Seahawks: Sam Darnold (glute) was cleared Friday and WILL start at Washington — no game designation. But both starting safeties are out: Julian Love (calf) and Ty Okada (hamstring). The app already lists Darnold as Seattle's expected starter, so its number has the quarterback news baked in.
Commanders: Marcus Mariota starts for Jayden Daniels, who is out with a dislocated elbow.
Giants: Jameis Winston starts; Jaxson Dart is on injured reserve and out for the season after knee surgery.
Titans: Cam Ward is Tennessee's starting quarterback — not a backup. No change there.

Ravens: left tackle Ronnie Stanley (toe) is ruled OUT — rookie Carson Vinson makes his first NFL start. Wide receiver Zay Flowers (hamstring) is questionable after practicing limited Friday. Defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike and linebacker Teddye Buchanan practiced fully all week with no designation and are set for their season debuts.
Cowboys: Cobie Durant, Malik Hooker, P.J. Locke and Demarvion Overshown are all out — none of them traveled to Rio.
Rams: Myles Garrett is on injured reserve after knee surgery and misses the Denver game.

Bears: Case Keenum is in line to start Monday night against Philadelphia. Caleb Williams (hamstring) is week-to-week and Tyson Bagent is still in the concussion protocol. The app caught up Friday night — it now shows Keenum, so its number for this game finally matches the news.
items.headline: Every injury that matters, in one place
paragraphs: That's the whole board — nothing scattered anywhere else in this brief. Read it once and you're caught up on who's in and who's out.
items.takeaway: News gets priced into the line within hours. The edge is knowing which news the line already ate.

items.headline: Rain at MetLife is the only real weather problem
paragraphs: Titans at Giants, 1 p.m. ET Sunday: rain showers through the game, temperatures near 68, wind 16 to 23 mph, and a 97% chance of rain. It's the wettest, windiest game on the board by a mile.

Everywhere else is fine. Friday's National Weather Service sweep found no other trouble spots: hot and humid but dry in Jacksonville and Miami, calm and sunny in Buffalo, Cleveland, Cincinnati, Santa Clara and Tampa, and a cool, clear evening in Denver for Sunday night football.
items.takeaway: Weather changes how the game is played, not who the better team is.

items.headline: The NFL's first Brazil game is Sunday
paragraphs: Ravens vs. Cowboys, 4:25 p.m. ET from Maracanã Stadium in Rio de Janeiro — the first regular-season NFL game ever played in Brazil.

Baltimore landed Friday morning and gets its first look at the stadium Saturday. On the field questions: the players' union chief said Friday that union and league field experts have monitored the surface all week and are working to make it as safe and playable as possible.
The app's board has Baltimore -3.5 at DraftKings with the total at 53.5 (52.5 at FanDuel) — the highest total on the Sunday board.
items.takeaway: New stadium, long flight, rookie left tackle making his first start. Weird games deserve smaller bets, not bigger opinions.

items.headline: What today's three cards actually say
paragraphs: The Balanced card is Vikings moneyline at -120 on DraftKings: risk $120 to win $100. The app's model says Minnesota wins about 59 times out of 100; the -120 price implies about 55. Small gap, medium confidence, 0.75 units.

The Hit Rate card is Giants moneyline at -135 on DraftKings: risk $135 to win $100. The model says the Giants win about 73 times out of 100; the price implies about 56. That's the biggest model-vs-price gap on the screen — but the app grades this one low confidence and prices it at negative expected value. A big gap alone is not a bet.

The Value card is Raiders +3 at +102 on DraftKings: risk $100 to win $102 if Las Vegas stays within a field goal or wins outright. The model says that happens about 50.5 times out of 100; the price implies about 47. This is the only one of the three the app prices as positive expected value (+3.6%), with medium confidence and 0.75 units.
items.takeaway: Every card shows the price AND the app's number. The gap between them — plus the app's own confidence grade — is the whole story.

items.headline: A line move is the market's price tag for the news
paragraphs: Seattle opened the week as a 5.5-point favorite at Washington. As the Darnold practice news spread, the line climbed to -7.5 at DraftKings. That two-point move is the market's price tag for the Darnold news — and on Friday the news became official: Darnold is cleared and will start.
Now check the app's number for the same game: the model has Seattle by 7.74. The market (-7.5) and the app (-7.74) agree. The Darnold news is fully priced — there is nothing left to chase there.

But Friday evening brought NEW news: both of Seattle's starting safeties, Julian Love and Ty Okada, were ruled out — after the app's last board snapshot. So the steps are: (1) the Darnold move already happened — don't pay for it twice; (2) the app's number matches the market, so the old news is done; (3) watch whether the line drifts back toward -7 before Sunday on the safeties news — that's the live question.
items.takeaway: The move IS the news, priced in points. Old news is priced. Only new news can move the number again.

items.headline: The biggest model-vs-market gap on the board is in Rio
paragraphs: The market has Baltimore -3.5 in Rio. The app's model says Dallas by 1.5. That's about five points of disagreement — wider than any other Sunday game.

The market has had since Friday afternoon to digest the Ravens' news: Stanley ruled out, a rookie making his first start at left tackle, Flowers a game-time call, a strange field, a long flight. It still says Baltimore by more than a field goal.

What to do with a gap like this: it's a reason to look closer, not a reason to bet Dallas. A five-point disagreement in a weird environment means stay small or stay away — not “the model says bet the Cowboys.”
items.takeaway: When the app and the market disagree by five points, that's the game to study — carefully.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: The app's three cards shuffled overnight
paragraphs: Balanced was Giants moneyline -130 on Friday; now it's Vikings moneyline -120. Hit Rate was Lions moneyline -298; now it's Giants moneyline -135. Value stayed on the Raiders +3 (now +102 at DraftKings).
The app also caught up on Chicago's quarterback: it flipped the Bears' expected starter from Bagent to Keenum on Friday night, so its Monday-night number finally matches the news.
items.takeaway: When the app's picks move, the news moved first. Read the move.

items.headline: Kansas City drifted toward Miami
paragraphs: The Chiefs were -11.5 on Wednesday. Friday evening's board has them -10 at DraftKings (-10.5 at FanDuel) — a point to a point-and-a-half of quiet drift toward the Dolphins, with no single headline behind it.
The app's model has Kansas City by only about 4, so the market and the model aren't close on this one either.
items.takeaway: Quiet moves without news are the ones to ask about — not chase.

items.headline: Check the board Sunday morning, not Saturday night
paragraphs: Three live things to re-check: the final MetLife forecast (rain timing decides how ugly that game gets), whether Seattle's line drifts on the safeties news, and the inactive lists 90 minutes before kickoff. If you like a number tonight, write it down — then compare it to Sunday's price before you bet.
items.takeaway: The best bet is often the same bet at a better price.

items.headline: Betting term of the day: steam
paragraphs: Steam is the word for a line moving fast across the sportsbooks — the market repricing in a hurry. Example: Seattle went from -5.5 to -7.5 in about a day after the Darnold practice news. That's steam.

Steam tells you the market moved. It doesn't tell you who moved it, or whether the new number is right. That's what the app's number is for — compare the steamed price against it before you decide anything.
items.takeaway: Steam is the market shouting. The app's number is the conversation.

article.title: NFL EDGE Saturday Morning Brief

evidence.fact: Seahawks QB Sam Darnold (glute) was cleared Friday and will start Sunday at Washington; coach Mike Macdonald confirmed it and Darnold carries no game designation after full practices Thursday and Friday. Starting safeties Julian Love (calf, hurt in Thursday practice) and Ty Okada (hamstring) were both ruled out.
evidence.interpretation: Seattle gets its starting QB back but loses both starting safeties against a Washington offense starting a backup QB.

evidence.fact: Ravens final designations for Sunday in Brazil: LT Ronnie Stanley (toe) is OUT; WR Zay Flowers (hamstring) was limited Friday and is QUESTIONABLE; DT Nnamdi Madubuike and LB Teddye Buchanan practiced fully all week with no game designation and are set for their season debuts. Rookie fifth-round pick Carson Vinson is expected to make his first NFL start at left tackle. Both teams held walkthroughs Friday, so the Friday report is an estimation.
evidence.interpretation: Baltimore's offensive line gets weaker while its defense gets two starters back; Flowers remains a game-time decision.

evidence.fact: The Bears are proceeding with third-stringer Case Keenum as the expected starter for Monday night vs. Philadelphia. Starter Caleb Williams (hamstring strain) is week-to-week and backup Tyson Bagent remains in the concussion protocol — he was back at the team facility Friday but did not practice. Keenum, 38, has not thrown a regular-season pass since 2023.
evidence.interpretation: Chicago is down to its third quarterback for a Monday night game against an undefeated Eagles team.

evidence.fact: Commanders QB Jayden Daniels is out (dislocated left elbow); Marcus Mariota starts vs. Seattle. Giants QB Jaxson Dart was placed on IR and will miss the rest of the season after knee surgery; Jameis Winston starts vs. Tennessee. The Rams placed edge rusher Myles Garrett on injured reserve after knee surgery; he misses Sunday's game at Denver and is out a minimum of four games.
evidence.interpretation: Two Sunday games feature backup quarterbacks; Denver's offense faces a Rams pass rush missing its best player.

evidence.fact: Four Cowboys did not travel to Rio and are ruled out for Sunday: CB Cobie Durant (hamstring), S Malik Hooker (forearm), S P.J. Locke (foot), LB Demarvion Overshown (hamstring). Both teams held walkthroughs Friday, so the Friday report is an estimation.
evidence.interpretation: Dallas's secondary is notably shorthanded for the Brazil game.

evidence.fact: Titans at Giants (MetLife, 1 p.m. ET Sunday): rain showers through the game, temperature near 68°F, wind 16 to 23 mph, chance of rain 97%. Rain runs from Saturday through Sunday night.
evidence.interpretation: MetLife is the only game where weather genuinely changes how football gets played.

evidence.fact: Friday's National Weather Service sweep of the other outdoor games found no trouble spots: hot and humid but dry in Jacksonville (85°F) and Miami (87°F); sunny and calm in Buffalo (68°F), Cleveland (70°F), Cincinnati (69°F) and Santa Clara (69°F); slight shower chance after 2 p.m. in Landover with wind 12-14 mph; cool and clear in Denver by the 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff (about 58°F).
evidence.interpretation: Weather is a non-factor everywhere except MetLife.

evidence.fact: Ravens vs. Cowboys kicks off Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET from Maracanã Stadium in Rio de Janeiro — the first regular-season NFL game ever played in Brazil. The Ravens arrived Friday morning and will visit the stadium for the first time on Saturday. NFLPA executive director JC Tretter said Friday that field experts from the union and the league monitored the surface all week and are working to make it as safe and playable as possible for Sunday.
evidence.interpretation: Unfamiliar surface, long travel, no practice time on the field — an unusual environment for both teams.
